featured_reviews.name: Prerna Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I happened to know about Chale Chalo through Instagram. At first I was apprehensive. I am not a usual cyclist, used to cycle in childhood. But I decided to take the plunge after Rohit’s reassurance that the tour is going to be on a slow pace and also a great experience. Like he had said this was indeed one of the best experiences I have had till date. The ride was super smooth, he helped us guide through traffic. We saw the scenic lanes of interior Vasai, visited the fort (thanks to this tour my gallery is filled with amazing pictures now), put up tents on Suruchi beach, played games (revived childhood) which was followed by a scrumptious lunch by Chale Chalo itself.
Not only this tour helped overcome my inhibitions of riding a cycle again but I also ended meeting amazing people that day.
You might see me joining in these tours often 😜.
All in all 10/10. LOVED IT! A big thanks to Rohit and Ayushi ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Namita Lulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Beach Hopping tour organised by the Chalo Chale team is a wholesome experience of spending time amidst nature. Everything from meals and views to safety and comfort is well taken care of and people from all age groups can equally enjoy. Thank you team Chalo Chale!

Both Rohit and Ayushi along with Prasobh in their team are wonderful tour guides who have thoughtfully curated this tour to help you make the most of your experience. We got to spend a good amount of time at every beach and had fun playing games like dog and the bone and mafia. The group setting and the vibes were all perfect and I'm already looking forward to being a part of many such tours now. If you're taking time out of your schedule to be a part of the Chalo Chale tours, you won't regret it for sure. 💃✨

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently went on a bicycle trip in Vasai and had a fantastic time. The trip was well-organized, Rohit and Ayushi, the team leads were friendly and helpful. They took us through the hidden lanes and bylanes of Vasai, and we got to see a side of the place that we wouldn't have otherwise. The route was picturesque, and the scenery was breathtaking.

I rode bicycle after 9 years and I was bit worried if I would able to complete the patch, however I found it easy and Chalo Chale team has backup to switch on scooty if tired.

I would definitely recommend this trip to anyone who loves nature and adventure.

Mumbai Heritage Walk is probably known as the ‘dream city’ and rightly so the city is indeed like a beautiful, magnificent dream. Old Mumbai is the part of Mumbai that represents its heritage and history. Reflecting on the time of Colonial era, the area is studded with numerous tourist attractions. From Chhatrapati Shivaji terminus to the ‘White town’ to the University library to the magnificent Marine drive, the city has so many spectacular attractions that one can never miss. Explore all these places of Old Mumbai and many more with this heritage walk tour.

Walking tours expose many residents and visitors to the structures.

featured_reviews.name: Lovie Chadha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vasai Fort offers a fascinating glimpse into the region’s rich history while providing a peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. The fort has a unique charm, and walking through its ruins allows you to truly appreciate the stories and heritage it holds.

The atmosphere is calm and relaxing, and the scenic surroundings make it a wonderful place to spend a few quiet hours exploring, reflecting, and enjoying nature. Whether you’re a history enthusiast, a photography lover, or simply looking for a serene outing, Vasai Fort is definitely worth a visit.

humble request to all visitors: let’s help preserve the beauty and heritage of this remarkable place by maintaining cleanliness and avoiding littering. Small actions from each of us can make a big difference in keeping this historic treasure beautiful for future generations.

featured_reviews.name: Dipak Sapkale Koli
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Vasai Fort (also known as Forte de Baçaim during Portuguese rule), and it is truly a majestic yet neglected piece of history. There is no entry ticket, which makes it easily accessible for everyone. You will find local food stalls inside and around the fort offering vada pav, bhel, gola, and soda sharbat. However, visitors must ensure they do not litter and help keep this heritage site clean.

Built by the Portuguese Empire in the 16th century, it served as a strategic naval base, administrative center, and trading hub on the western coast. The fort remained under Portuguese control for nearly two centuries until it was captured by the Marathas under Chimaji Appa in 1739. Later, it passed into the hands of the British East India Company, marking another significant shift in power. Its construction reflects military brilliance, with a massive boundary wall stretching nearly 4 km.

Inside the fort, you can see magnificent church ruins, old barracks, market areas, bell towers, and beautifully crafted spiral stone staircases — all showcasing remarkable Indo-Portuguese architecture. The Mandwa Gate stands tall as a historic entrance, and the surroundings also include the revered Vajreshwari Temple and Hanuman Temple.

However, despite being under the Archaeological Survey of India, the site appears poorly maintained and largely ignored. Trees are growing out of the fort walls, weakening the structure, and no visible effort is made to clear them. Sadly, some miscreants have written their names on the walls, further damaging this heritage monument which is again ignored by Archeological Survey of India.

History needs to be cared for, restored, and respected — Vasai Fort deserves preservation worthy of its glorious past.

featured_reviews.name: Manoj Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text: Vasai Fort is a lovely, quiet spot to spend an evening. The historic ruins, dating back to the Portuguese era, is surrounded by greenery. It’s not crowded, making it perfect for a peaceful stroll or simply relaxing. The cool breeze and serene atmosphere make it a great place to unwind. If you're looking for a calm and scenic place to escape the hustle, Vasai Fort is definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Vasai Fort (also known as Fort Bassein) is an awesome historical site near Mumbai. The massive ruins give a cool glimpse into Portuguese architecture and history. The vibe is pretty epic – great for photos, exploring old walls, and soaking in the local legends. If you’re into heritage and scenic views, Vasai Fort is totally worth a visit! 😎

Vasai Fort's history began in the 15th century as a strategic hub for the Sultan of Gujarat, but it is most famously associated with the Portuguese who conquered and rebuilt it in the 1530s, making it their main naval base in Western India for over two centuries. It was eventually captured by the Marathas under Chimaji Appa in 1739.
The fort is ruined and mostly full of couples doing photoshoot the fort is protected by Archeological survey of India the authority should maintain cleanliness .
You can get a bus from vasai station to virar killa 10 rupees per person last bus will be at 9:00 PM.

featured_reviews.name: shaurya Jamsandekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently, I visited Vasai Fort with my friends. It is a historically significant site surrounded by lush greenery, offering a peaceful and scenic environment for visitors. The architecture and ruins reflect its rich past and make it an interesting place to explore, especially for history enthusiasts and photographers.

However, the maintenance of the fort requires considerable improvement. Several areas appear neglected, and better preservation efforts from the authorities would greatly enhance the overall experience.

Overall, Vasai Fort is a worthwhile destination for its heritage value and natural surroundings, but improved upkeep is necessary to fully realize its potential.

featured_reviews.name: Kushal Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)
Vasai Fort / वसईचा किल्ला — Vasai West 🏰🌿

As someone born and brought up in Vasai, this place isn’t just a tourist spot for me — it’s a part of my life, my childhood, my memories, and my identity. 🫶
I’ve visited this fort more than 100–200 times, and every single visit still feels special.
वसईचा किल्ला holds a deep emotional place in every वसईकर’s heart. ❤️

This fort is vast, beautiful, historic and full of peace. 🌳
It’s surrounded by lush green trees on all sides, and one end of the fort touches the famous Vasai Dock. ⚓
If you’re into history, nature, photography, or even just calm vibes — this place is perfect. ☀️📸✨

History & Pride 🏹

This fort has seen the legacy of Marathas, Peshwas, and the Portuguese.
It is especially known for Chimaji Appa (brother of Bajirao Peshwa), who fought and reclaimed this fort back from the Portuguese. 🛡️🔥
The entrance itself greets you with his statue — a reminder of bravery and pride. ✨🗿

Why This Place is Special 🤍

I have come here with:

Friends 👬

Parents 👪

Cousins 👭

School picnics 🎒

Even solo, just for peace 🌿😌

For every phase of my life, this fort has always been there.

Cultural Importance 🎬

Many movies and songs have been shot here —
Most recently, a song from Kantara Chapter 1 was filmed here. 🎥
This place is loved by locals, tourists, and Mumbaikars alike. 🏞️

Must-See Inside 🔍

The massive stone walls 🧱

Huge open courtyards 🏞️

Old Portuguese structures 🕍

The Watch Tower – चक्री जिना (a must-visit + very photogenic 👀📸)

If you plan to explore the entire fort properly, keep at least half a day — it’s truly big. 🕒

Final Words 💛

This is not just a fort.
It’s a feeling. A memory. A connection. 🌙
If you are coming to Vasai — you cannot miss वसईचा किल्ला. 🌿

Highly recommended. 🤍
5/5 — Always. Forever. ⭐️

featured_reviews.name: Unmesh Birje
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imelda Lake is a charmingly small and serene spot, ideal for those looking to escape the hustle and bustle of daily life. Its tranquility and picturesque setting make it a perfect place for quiet contemplation or a peaceful walk.

However, it's important to note that access to the water is restricted. Visitors cannot enter the lake waters due to the presence of animals being bathed there. This limitation might be disappointing for those looking forward to a more interactive experience with the lake.

Adjacent to the lake is a temple, which is a haven of peace and serenity. The temple's tranquil environment adds to the overall calming experience of the visit. It's a great place for those seeking a moment of reflection or spiritual connection.

In summary, while Imelda Lake offers a serene and beautiful environment, the restrictions on water access may be a drawback for some. Nevertheless, the peaceful atmosphere, especially around the temple, makes it a worthwhile visit for those seeking tranquility.

featured_reviews.name: Shashank Sapaliga
featured_reviews.review_text: Dongri Fort is a very beautiful, calm and peaceful small Lookout Fortress , not many people know about this Place but offers scenic views of Buildings and Hills of Mira-Bhayandar and Vasai-Virar. Vasai Creek meets Arabian Sea right a few metres ahead of this Scenic Spot, was probably built during the Portuguese Era and had places to keep barrels for controlling Foreign invasions. The Only remains are the Outer Boundary Wall and The Houses inside the  Wall. Please maintain the sanctity, Cleanliness and History of the lookout Fortress, it is currently under CCTV Camera Surveillance to curb illegal activities happening especially at night !

review_photos.caption: Views of High Rise Buildings  of Vasai West from Fortress
Views of Vasai Creek meeting Arbian Sea

featured_reviews.name: Krishnendu Mondal
featured_reviews.review_text: It is a peaceful place, away from city noise and pollution. The roadways to reach the place is not good and the fort was not maintained. The people are very friendly and nearby view is very nice. The park was closed today (Saturday), opens from 4 pm.

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Chavan.
featured_reviews.review_text: Dongri Fort popularly known as dhara I fort is nearest fort to strong vasai fort. Portuguese built this fort as support fort for vasai fort. This fort is in two steps first is near to sea where Portuguese offices and checkpoint also jetty on nearby hill is it's main fort but nowadays the main fort is totally ruined now there is a garden. When marathas attacked on vasai they understood that if they first win dharavi fort then it's easy to win vasai so they first win dharavi fort. Other things to see old time bela Mata church, old water tank, chirekban ie stone khadan. You can easily visit this place with family and friends.

featured_reviews.name: Vishalkumar Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
This location is ideal for cyclists, photographers, or anyone looking to escape the city and reconnect with nature. Highly recommended for an early morning adventure!
The real highlight, however, was the stunning view of the sea from the fort. As the sun broke through the clouds, the sky looked absolutely magical — with birds flying, boats dotting the shore, and a golden light bathing the horizon. It was a breathtaking moment that made the climb totally worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Lokhande

I believe this fort was used as a watch tower. There is one huge Sacred fig tree and underneath that you will find a Shivling.

Just ahead to that there is a place where you can stand an you can observe the entire end to end shore and it was beautiful to see. You will sit and enjoy the view for hours..

Fort is now in ruins, but right now efforts are been made by the authorities to keep it clean.

Best time to visit it will be sunset and early morning.
